summary.text: 等 is conventionally analyzed as a compound with 竹 marking a bamboo-related category and 寺 serving as a sound component. Its earliest supported gloss is “orderly bamboo slips”; historical and current uses include “equal,” rank or class, “and so forth,” and “wait.”

formation.text: The conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 竹 contributes a bamboo-related meaning, while 寺 supplies a sound cue. A competing interpretation treats the graph as semantic, linking bamboo slips with orderly arrangement. The early gloss and that interpretation do not prove how the graph was first created.

components.text: 竹 contributes the bamboo category. The early gloss 齊簡 (“orderly bamboo slips”) connects the character with bamboo slips used for writing. No distinct earlier form of 竹 within 等 is established.

寺 is conventionally identified as the phonetic component. Its sound-series association with 等 supports that role, although the reconstructed forms differ and do not settle the precise correspondence. Debate about 寺’s own origin concerns that graph’s history, not its role in 等.

sound_limitation.text: The sound-series evidence supports a phonetic relationship, but the cited reconstructions do not establish the exact historical correspondence that motivated it.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese reconstruction, 寺 is *ljɯs and 等 is *tɯːŋʔ. The differing forms support sound-series membership but not exact sound identity.

history.text: The earliest forms identified in the paleographic account date to the Warring States period and contain 竹 and 寺; some also show an added 口. The account reports no known oracle-bone or bronze forms, which describes its record rather than the date when the graph was created.

The received Shuowen entry analyzes 等 as 从竹从寺 and associates 寺 with the even ordering of official ranks. A later commentary interprets 齊簡 as arranging bamboo slips evenly. Another account classifies 等 as semantic, while dictionaries assign 寺 a phonetic role.
䓁 is recorded as a later variant associated with clerical-script variation in the top of 竹; it is not an ancestor of 等.

uncertainties.text: The conventional phonetic analysis and a competing semantic interpretation are both represented, so the graph’s original formation remains unsettled. Reconstructions support a sound-series relationship between 寺 and 等 without resolving the precise historical correspondence.
Proposed links between 等 and 登, and to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *tVŋ, are not independently established in the cited specialist evidence.

It rejects a proposal that 寺 itself was borrowed for 志 based on sound resemblance alone. This is a debate about 寺 and related graphs; it does not directly refute the later compound analysis of 等 as containing 寺 phonetic.
evidence.title: 楊樹達文字訓解六則及其釋字理論商榷

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, entry 等
evidence.text: The dictionary treats 䓁 as a variant of 等, citing its occurrence in the Kong He stele as reported in 《隸辨》. It explains that clerical-script 竹 tops were sometimes written like 艸 and later could be confused or used interchangeably. This is a later variant-form relation, not evidence for an ancestor of the base graph 等.
evidence.title: [A02997] 等 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 金真姬,《常用漢字二百字探源》
evidence.text: This secondary account reports no known oracle-bone or bronze attestations for 等. Its earliest listed forms are Warring States examples, including Baoshan and Guodian manuscripts. Some examples have 竹 and 寺; some also show an added 口. It gives the Shuowen gloss 齊簡也 and discusses a possible progression from arranging slips to equality and rank. These are reported attestations and an interpretation, not proof of when the graph was created or a chronology for every sense. The account classifies the graph as 会意, in contrast to dictionaries that treat 寺 as phonetic.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen definition 齊簡也 and its analysis 从竹从寺, followed by the claim 寺，官曹之等平也. It also gives Duan Yucai’s later interpretation: arranging bamboo slips evenly, extended to things being even and then to ranks. This is a historical lexicographic explanation and later commentary; neither independently proves the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 等 děng - 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學
evidence.text: The page presents a phono-semantic analysis with 竹 as semantic and 寺 as phonetic, alongside a bamboo-slip explanation. It lists examples associated with class/order, rank, steps, equality and waiting. Its waiting example is attributed to the Tang poem 小兒詩. These citations attest uses in the cited texts but do not establish that every sense arose in the order displayed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫, 等

evidence.text: The entry identifies 竹 as the semantic component and 寺 as phonetic. It gives Mandarin Pinyin děng and Cantonese Jyutping dang2. Its phonetic-series data in Zhengzhang Shangfang’s Old Chinese system lists 寺 *ljɯs and two 等 readings, *tɯːʔ and *tɯːŋʔ. The same page gives 等 as Middle Chinese tongX and Old Chinese *tˤəŋʔ in Baxter–Sagart (2014). These are system-specific reconstructions, not observed speech; the readings do not show exact sound identity. The page’s further proposal that 寺 was later borrowed for another word is not independently established by the inspected sources.
evidence.title: 等 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The 寺 phonetic-series listing includes 等 and gives 寺 *ljɯs and 等 *tɯːŋʔ in the displayed Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese system. This supports a series relationship while showing that the reconstructed forms differ. Reconstructions vary by system and do not alone establish the exact historical sound correspondence.
evidence.title: 寺 - 聲符 - 上古音系 - 韻典網

evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin sì and Cantonese zi6 for 寺. Its modern pronunciation is not by itself evidence for why 寺 could function as a phonetic in 等. For comparison within a stated reconstruction system, the inspected Zhengzhang data gives 寺 *ljɯs, while Baxter–Sagart (2014) data gives 寺 /*s-[d]əʔ-s/ and 等 /*tˤəŋʔ/. Those system-specific forms differ; series membership and the dictionary analysis support a phonetic role, but the precise historical correspondence remains unresolved.
evidence.title: 寺 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: 王安碩,《楊樹達文字訓解六則及其釋字理論商榷》
evidence.text: This article reports and argues for a disputed analysis of 寺: it proposes that the bronze graph comprises 又 and a 止 phonetic element, and that later graphic change contributed to the received Shuowen analysis of 寸 plus 之. The dispute concerns 寺’s own graphic history. It does not directly refute the conventional later analysis of 寺 as the phonetic component in 等.
evidence.title: 楊樹達文字訓解六則及其釋字理論商榷

evidence.text: The entry reproduces the received Shuowen analysis of 寺 as 廷也，有法度者也 and 从寸之聲. This is the traditional lexicographic account; it differs from a modern scholarly proposal that the early graph has 又 and 止. The inspected sources do not establish an earlier positional form of 寺 within 等.
evidence.title: 寺 sì - 汉典

evidence.text: The museum page describes the Baoshan Chu slips as excavated from tomb 2 and dates them broadly to the Warring States period (475–221 BCE). This gives archaeological context for the manuscript source named in the paleographic account; it does not itself identify or reproduce a particular 等 glyph image.

evidence.text: The entry records 䓁 as a variant of 等 and discusses later clerical-script variation in the top component. It also lists senses including equality, rank, enumeration and waiting. This is evidence for a later variant and a sense inventory, not for an ancestor of 等 or a chronology of its senses.

evidence.text: The entry presents 等 as a phono-semantic graph with 竹 as semantic and 寺 as phonetic, and gives Japanese readings including on-reading トウ and kun-readings ひとしい and など. It proposes an orderly-slip explanation and semantic extensions to equality and rank. This is a modern dictionary account, not evidence for a Japanese-created origin.
evidence.title: 等

evidence.text: The entry classifies 等 as phono-semantic with 寺 as sound element and discusses ordering wooden slips as a proposed original sense. It describes later use in a waiting sense associated with 待. This supports reporting a possible relationship or writing usage, but does not independently date the first 等 waiting use or prove a single semantic path.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

A waiting-related use is cited in a transmitted Tang poem. The earliest dated 等 use meaning ‘wait’ remains unresolved. Manuscript spellings of 待 with 寺 do not attest 等 meaning ‘wait’.

The proposed link between 等 and 待 for the waiting sense is not independently established here as a specific borrowing event. The source word’s graphic and sound histories do not by themselves date the borrowing.

The earliest depicted referent or name underlying 寺’s own graphic origin remains disputed. That uncertainty concerns 寺’s origin and does not by itself invalidate its independently attested phonetic-series role in 等.
The proposed relationship to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *tVŋ and derivation from 登 in imported material were not independently verified in the inspected primary or specialist sources.

No positional ancestor form distinct from the components 竹 and 寺 in 等 was established. Both components therefore have empty origin_form and origin_relation none; no chronology is inferred from shape or role.
